obligation: Bank notification incident (OCC)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, the bank's ability to deliver products or services to a material portion of its customers, or a business line whose failure would cause material loss (includes incidents that start in an affiliate)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident has occurred
notify: OCC supervisory office or OCC-designated point of contact (email, telephone, or other method the OCC prescribes)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - scenario: business wire and ACH initiation suspended for about 310,000 bank business users for 5.5 hours on a business day; determination recorded Day 0 13:40
notifying_entity: Bank (determination officials: Group CISO with the bank chief operations officer)

obligation: Holding company notification incident (Federal Reserve)
trigger: Notification incident affecting the bank holding company, including a business line whose failure would cause material loss (here the platform service for 310 client institutions)
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the holding company determines a notification incident has occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - separate determination recorded Day 0 14:30
notifying_entity: Holding company (Group General Counsel with the Group Chief Risk Officer)

obligation: Bank service provider notice to OCC-supervised client banks
trigger: Provider determines a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, covered services for 4 or more hours (not previously communicated maintenance, 53.4(b))
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Each affected client's bank-designated point of contact (53.4(a)(1)); if none, its CEO and CIO or two comparable individuals (53.4(a)(2))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 74 OCC-supervised client banks; 4-hour mark at Day 0 15:15
notifying_entity: Financial Software division (client risk and assurance director)

obligation: Bank service provider notice to the bank itself (affiliate as provider)
trigger: Same trigger; the bank is a banking organization customer of the division
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: The bank's designated point of contact (none given yet; P03 G-041), otherwise the bank's CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the bank is the platform's largest tenant

obligation: Bank service provider notice to state member bank clients
trigger: Same trigger for clients supervised by the Federal Reserve
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Each client's designated contact, or CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 31 state member bank clients

obligation: Bank service provider notice to FDIC-supervised client banks
trigger: Same trigger for FDIC-supervised clients
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Each client's designated contact, or CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 107 FDIC-supervised clients

obligation: Credit union client notice (contract)
citation: Client master agreements; credit unions' own duty under 12 CFR 748.1(c)
trigger: Security incident or disruption affecting the platform service
deadline: Contract term (5 business days today; POAM-022); send with the bank notices in practice so credit unions can meet their own 72-hour NCUA reporting
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 98 credit union clients (no federal service provider notice rule applies to the division for them)

obligation: Client contract security incident notice
citation: Client master agreements (24 hours in 88 contracts; 72 hours standard)
trigger: Security incident affecting the client's tenant or data (support console read access to every tenant's configuration and user lists)
deadline: Per contract: within 24 hours or 72 hours of the division becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all 310 clients (tenant configuration and business user contact lists were readable)

obligation: Notice to client banks whose customers' data was exposed (conversion files)
citation: Client contracts; 12 CFR 30 App. B Supplement A II.A.2 (client banks' guidance on service provider notice)
trigger: Unauthorized access to client banks' customer information held by the division (2025 conversion files in a compromised mailbox: about 31,200 consumers of 2 client banks)
deadline: As soon as possible; contract terms (24 hours for one client, 72 hours for the other)
notify: The two client banks' security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - scenario

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent maintaining personal information for a covered entity has a breach
deadline: Within 10 days following determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: The covered entity (each affected client bank)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for Florida residents among the 31,200 consumers; apply each other state's agent rules the same way

obligation: Client banks' own notices (their decisions)
citation: 12 CFR 53.3, 225.302, 304.23 (client banks); Supplement A II.A.1.b and III (client banks); state breach laws
trigger: Each client decides whether it has a notification incident or a customer notice duty
deadline: Each client's own clocks
applies_at_this_tier: Not the group's duty; the division supplies facts, counts by state, and a notice template on request

obligation: Regulator notice of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information (bank)
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B Supplement A II.A.1.b (guidance)
trigger: Bank becomes aware of unauthorized access to or use of sensitive customer information (for example, name with an account number, or a user name and password)
deadline: As soon as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario - the support console exposed bank business users' contact data only; re-decide if forensics finds more. Covered in the 53.3 notice in any case

obligation: Bank customer notice under the response program
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B Supplement A III.A to III.C (guidance)
trigger: Misuse of sensitive customer information has occurred or is reasonably possible
deadline: As soon as possible; delay only on a written law enforcement request
applies_at_this_tier: Not triggered in this scenario (as above). The bank still sends a phishing warning to its business users whose contact data was readable (a customer service choice)

obligation: Holding company response program (nonbank subsidiaries)
trigger: Unauthorized access to customer information of the holding company or a nonbank subsidiary
deadline: As soon as possible (Federal Reserve notice and customer notice as Supplement A describes)
applies_at_this_tier: Limited - guarantor data is not GLBA customer information (commercial credit); state breach laws govern those notices. The 225.302 notice covers the incident

obligation: Suspicious activity report (bank)
trigger: Known or suspected federal criminal violation involving a transaction conducted through the bank (the $14.2 million funding wire)
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection; up to 30 more days to identify a suspect, never more than 60 days after initial detection
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the bank released the wire. SAR existence is confidential (21.11(k))

obligation: Immediate notice of an ongoing violation
trigger: A reportable violation that needs immediate attention, such as an ongoing fraud
deadline: Immediately, by telephone, in addition to the timely SAR
notify: Appropriate law enforcement authority and the OCC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker is still active (fake remittance emails were still arriving on Day 0)

obligation: Board notice of SAR filing (bank)
trigger: A SAR is filed
deadline: Promptly after filing
notify: Bank board of directors or its designated committee
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Suspicious activity report (nonbank subsidiaries)
trigger: Suspected federal criminal violation against or through a nonbank subsidiary
deadline: Per 12 CFR 208.62 time limits
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for CRE Lending (fraud against it); the Financial Software division considers one for the vendor-impersonation emails. BSA/AML Officers coordinate with the bank filing; counsel confirms whether one report can cover both
notifying_entity: CRE Lending and Financial Software (nonbank BSA/AML Officer)

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire and invoice payments from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; fast reporting improves the chance of freezing funds
notify: FBI through ic3.gov; local FBI field office for large losses
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but required by POL-03 4.8
notifying_entity: Bank payments operations with the BSA/AML Officer

obligation: Wire recall request to the beneficiary bank
citation: Payment system practice; funds transfer agreement (contract)
trigger: A wire the bank sent is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery, before the beneficiary bank releases funds
notify: Beneficiary bank (phone to its wire or fraud department, then in writing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - most time-critical step; $9.8 million frozen in the scenario

obligation: Loss allocation for an unauthorized payment order
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.202 and 670.204 (UCC Article 4A as enacted in Florida; worked example)
trigger: A payment order accepted in the customer's name that the customer says it did not authorize
deadline: Refund with interest if the order was not authorized and not effective as the customer's order; counsel decides under 670.202
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - intercompany: CRE Lending's own authorized users approved the wire and the bank followed the agreed security procedure (MFA, dual approval, callback to the customer's designated contact), so the order is likely effective as CRE Lending's. Counsel decides

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents (guarantors' names with Social Security or account numbers in the compromised closer mailbox)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15-day extension only for good cause, and only for this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 610 Florida guarantors

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (no extension)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 610 Florida guarantors

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Counsel decides - 610 Florida guarantors, about 1,860 guarantors in all states

obligation: Other states' breach laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (each state where affected individuals reside)
trigger: Guarantors in 13 other states; client banks' consumers (client banks decide)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply each state's law to the guarantors' states of residence (POAM-023 adds a state field so counts are fast next time)

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Decision required - disclosure committee convened Day 0; determined not material on Day 3 (section 6 of the runbook); revisit if facts change

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - consider the incident and the resulting program changes in the next description of risk management and governance

obligation: Risk limit breach protocol (bank)
trigger: A cyber or fraud event breaches the risk appetite statement or a front line limit
deadline: Per the bank's breach protocol (informing the board, independent risk management, internal audit, and the OCC by severity)
notify: Bank board risk committee; OCC as the protocol requires
applies_at_this_tier: Checked - $4.4 million unrecovered loss does not breach the $25 million annual payment-instruction fraud limit; recorded

obligation: Cyber insurance and financial institution bond notice
trigger: Loss or suspected loss from fraud or a security incident
deadline: Per policy; notify the carriers before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Not in this scenario (no ransom); kept for extortion scenarios (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary reporting only). Recheck when a final rule is published
clock_starts: Not applicable until a final rule

obligation: FDIC notification incident rule (for the group)
trigger: Notification incident at an FDIC-supervised institution
deadline: 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's primary federal regulator is the OCC (Part 53 applies). FDIC-supervised client banks decide their own

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers at an FTC-jurisdiction financial institution
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - no group entity is under FTC Safeguards Rule jurisdiction (P03 section 1.1)

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident and extortion payment
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity
deadline: 72 hours after determination; 24 hours after an extortion payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - no New York-licensed entity

obligation: SEC Reg S-P customer notification
trigger: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information at a broker-dealer, investment company, investment adviser, or transfer agent
deadline: No later than 30 days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: No - no such entity in the group

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (as adopted by states)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - no insurance licensee in the group

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No for the group; the 98 credit union clients decide their own reports, using the division's notice

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the group holds no federal contracts
